decisions.executionNote: Coin is in the left workspace this episode. Begin elbow-up left-arm approach with gripper open; estimate holder location from head view.
Advance left arm toward the central-left holder while rotating to a downward coin pinch; maintain clearance over the bank.
Continue smooth inward approach with elbow-up posture. Aim above the coin before final wrist alignment and descent.
Bring left wrist over the holder; rotate toward vertical approach with jaws aligned to the coin's visible plane.
Finish vertical wrist alignment above the coin and approach cautiously with open jaws.
Use a small image-guided lateral correction toward the coin in the left wrist view; keep height and orientation fixed to assess alignment.
Center the coin between open fingertips using the observed wrist-image response. Keep vertical clearance until lateral alignment is confirmed.
Coin is nearly centered. Match its plane with a small yaw correction, lower four millimeters, and begin closing the left gripper.
Make a final few-millimeter lateral correction while closing around the coin; check contact visually before lifting.
Close fully on the centered coin and make a short test lift, checking separation from the holder.
Lift vertically with the left gripper closed, watching for the coin to remain between the fingers and clear the holder.
Pause to verify retention: the coin appears displaced from the fingertips after lifting, so grasp success is uncertain.
The coin is no longer retained. Open the left gripper and reposition above its observed new location for a recovery grasp.
Coin has settled flat and is centered laterally. Lower the open jaws vertically for an edge recovery grasp.
Lower to the flat coin's rim and correct the small rightward wrist-image offset while narrowing the jaws.
Gently close around the flat coin's opposing rim edges at table height; assess whether it is captured rather than pushed.
Close fully on the rim and perform a slow two-centimeter test lift to verify retention.
The flat coin remains centered between the jaws during the test lift. Raise it clear of the table and start moving left toward the bank.
Coin remains retained. Reorient its flat face toward a vertical insertion plane while transporting left, keeping clearance above the bank.
Continue carrying the retained coin leftward at safe height, gradually rotating its face vertical to match the bank slot.
Move above the bank's left-side slot while continuing the smooth rotation of the securely retained coin toward vertical.
Finish the coin's vertical orientation and approach above the bank, leaving ample height before precision alignment.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller increments. Finish vertical coin orientation and approach the slot without a large base-joint change.
Lower the vertical coin toward the bank and shift slightly left. Keep the grip closed and use the next view for precise slot alignment.
The coin and slot appear laterally aligned. Continue a slow vertical approach, preserving the current arm branch and checking clearance.
Descend in millimeter increments with a small lateral and yaw correction toward the slot center; keep the coin clamped.
Refine front-to-back slot alignment and lower slowly, leaving a short gravity insertion distance rather than pressing the gripper into the bank.
Release the vertical coin over the aligned slot without further downward pressure; inspect whether it drops cleanly inside.
Allow the released coin to settle into the slot, then lift the open gripper slightly for visual confirmation.
The coin landed flat on the bank rather than inside. Raise the open gripper for a safe recovery approach from above.
Use smaller upward increments after the continuity rejection; clear the bank before rotating for recovery.
Arc upward and forward while gradually turning the left gripper downward, maintaining clearance from the coin on the bank.
Continue the clearance arc into an overhead recovery pose, with open jaws and continuous elbow-up motion.
Continue turning toward an overhead pinch while keeping the fingertips above the bank surface.
Refine the downward wrist orientation above the bank and advance toward the coin without descending yet.
Complete the overhead orientation with open jaws and inspect coin-to-fingertip alignment before lowering.
Coin is centered laterally in the overhead view. Lower toward its rim while preserving the continuous elbow-up configuration.
Correct the coin's leftward wrist-image offset and approach its rim with partly open jaws; avoid contacting the bank.
Center the coin between the jaws and lower the final few millimeters for a careful rim grasp on the bank surface.
Close completely and perform a short vertical test lift to check whether the recovered coin is retained.
Test retention with a slow, short lift; the coin has tilted and may not yet be securely held.
The coin stayed on the bank. Reopen and lower the jaws to straddle its rim rather than closing above it.
Lower six millimeters to engage the coin's opposing rim edges, then close gently without pushing the bank.
Ease the jaws upward slightly to clear the curved bank surface while closing on the coin rim; verify retention before transport.
Coin slipped to the far side of the jaws. Open, gain slight clearance, and recenter over its observed position.
The coin is sliding down the bank's far side. Keep the jaws open and gain a clear overhead view of its settling position.
Approach the coin after it settles beside the bank, using an open overhead grasp and checking bank clearance.
Narrow the open jaws to clear the bank's side, center above the coin, and resume a cautious vertical approach.
Straighten the downward approach and lower the partly open jaws beside the bank, monitoring clearance and coin centering.
The bank crowds one jaw. Lift slightly and turn the pinch direction to obtain clearance along its side before trying again.
Continue turning the jaws parallel to the bank edge while lowering gradually toward the settled coin.
Finish aligning the pinch along the bank edge and move slightly away from the bank as the jaws approach the coin.
Center the settled coin and lower the jaws toward its rim, keeping the pinch direction parallel to the bank edge.
Close slowly around the centered coin rim, with only a two-millimeter descent; inspect retention before lifting.
The coin shifted instead of being captured. Reopen, recenter on its new position, and lower the pads to the table-level rim.
Relieve table contact slightly, place the coin rim within the pads, and close before another short retention test.
Lift only two centimeters with the gripper closed to determine whether the rim is captured.
The coin is not securely captured. Reopen and refine both depth and fore-aft alignment so the flat rim meets the pads rather than their tips.
Clear the bank by approaching from its far side with a slight wrist tilt, keeping the fingertip region near the coin and the bulky gripper body away.
With both jaws clear of the bank, lower the tilted gripper to the coin rim and narrow the opening gradually.
Engage the flat coin's rim with a small fore-aft correction and six-millimeter descent while closing carefully.
Close fully and make a slow two-centimeter test lift, checking the coin stays between the pads.
